cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Approve the Cover Story
cards.instruction: Get someone to endorse an explanation that protects the plan, reputation, or people involved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Can you approve 'delivery delay' in the newsletter? I don't want our new volunteer blamed for the melted cake. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She delivered it on time. We left it by the radiator.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Then 'storage problem'. Will you approve that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if we mention the refund.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely. 'Storage problem; full refund arranged.' Can I put your name under it?

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 revises explanation and A5 accepts refund for named approval, so the core negotiates support while protecting a volunteer under the added rank wording.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 explicitly corrects delivery delay with timely arrival and radiator storage; A3 accepts that correction instead of establishing the false claim as fact.

relationship.evidence: B2 protects the volunteer from a misleading explanation and B4 requires compensation mentioned.

heightening.evidence: B4 refund condition causes A5 new public wording and a signature request.

specificity.evidence: A1 newsletter, cake and volunteer establish the reputational stakes; B2 identifies actual responsibility.

brevityWit.evidence: A1 voluntary please and A3 authority slogan are redundant; A5 arranged refund should be made an explicit action if it is not already done.
